items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And unfortunately the guitar player was unable to play, Al Nevins, and I jumped in and subbed for him.

ctx.x: Didn’t someone record that with words later on?

The Platters, yeah. But they came on it and I had known them because they were guests on the Vaughn Monroe Show. And unfortunately the guitar player was unable to play, Al Nevins, and I jumped in and subbed for him. I put on his gray tuxedo and played on his D’Angelico guitar which I still have. And in the evening they asked me to play at the Astor Hotel — everything was a block away. I lived two blocks away at The Woodby on 45th Street. Kate Smith was on 44th Street and the Astor was between us.
You just walked to all these gigs.

items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: I subbed for the guitar player on the Three Suns, Morty (sic) [Al] Nevins, and I took his place.

ctx.x: Oh that’s so interesting to me.

Well I figured the life of a musician comes in phases. It started with the big bands for me. I thought when the band broke up that was the end of the world. It wasn’t. I went on staff, I did the “Kate Smith Show.” While I was on the “Kate Smith Show” I subbed for the guitar player on the Three Suns, Morty (sic) [Al] Nevins, and I took his place. I put his tux on and I appeared as him. And I ended up playing with them for two years. I went to Vegas the first six weeks we were married we were in Vegas and we played…
